You can make a color swatch in HTML in two main ways: using the built-in color picker input or by creating a custom element using HTML and CSS. [^1][^2][^3][^4]
[^1][^2][^3][^4]

1. Using the HTML Color Picker Input () [^5]
[^5]

The easiest way to create a functional color swatch that opens a native color picker is using the  element. This approach is simple and widely supported in modern browsers. [^5][^6][^7][^8][^9]
[^5][^6][^7][^8][^9]

HTML:

• The  attribute renders a small color swatch on the page.
• The  attribute sets the initial color, which must be a seven-character hexadecimal notation (e.g.,  for red). If no value is specified, it defaults to black (). [^5][^10][^11][^12]
[^5][^10][^11][^12]


You can track changes to the selected color using JavaScript event listeners. [^13]
[^13]

2. Creating a Custom Color Swatch with HTML and CSS
For more control over the appearance and functionality (e.g., displaying specific colors as part of a product list), you can use HTML and CSS to build custom elements. [^14][^15][^16][^17]
[^14][^15][^16][^17]

HTML:
CSS:
This method uses  elements and applies the desired color using the  CSS property, accepting various color values like HEX, RGB, or HSL. [^18][^19][^20][^21][^22]
[^18][^19][^20][^21][^22]

For inspiration on different styles and implementations, you can explore a visual gallery of color swatch designs using image search tools. [^23][^24]
[^23][^24]

The CSS<span> </span></div><code>minmax()</code><span> </span>function is<span> </span>a powerful tool used in<span> </span><strong>CSS Grid layout</strong><span> </span>to define a size range (a minimum and a maximum size) for a grid track (row or column). This allows for highly flexible and responsive designs without needing traditional media queries.



<h2>Usage and Syntax</h2>


The<span> </span><code>minmax()</code><span> </span>function is used within the<span> </span><code>grid-template-columns</code>,<span> </span><code>grid-template-rows</code>,<span> </span><code>grid-auto-columns</code>, or<span> </span><code>grid-auto-rows</code><span> </span>properties.



<pre class="language-css"><code class="language-css">
.container {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: minmax(min, max);
}
</code></pre>

<h2>Parameters and Values</h2>


The<span> </span><code>minmax(min, max)</code><span> </span>function accepts two arguments: a minimum value and a maximum value. Both can be various length units or keywords:<span><span><span> </span>


<ul><li><span><code>&lt;length&gt;</code>: Fixed units like<span> </span><code>px</code>,<span> </span><code>em</code>,<span> </span><code>rem</code>, etc.</span></li><li><span><code>&lt;percentage&gt;</code>: Relative to the size of the grid container. If the container's size depends on its tracks, percentages are treated as<span> </span><code>auto</code>.</span></li><li><span><code>min-content</code>: Represents the smallest possible size the content can take without overflowing (e.g., the width of the longest unbreakable word).</span></li>
<li><span><code>max-content</code>: Represents the largest possible size the content would take without any line breaks.</span></li><li><span><code>auto</code>:</span><ul><li><span>As a minimum, it represents the largest minimum size (as specified by<span> </span><code>min-width</code><span> </span>or<span> </span><code>min-height</code>) of the grid items.</span></li><li><span>As a maximum, it is identical to<span> </span><code>max-content</code>.</span></li></ul></li><li><span><code>&lt;flex&gt;</code><span> </span>(<code>fr</code><span> </span>units)</strong>: A fractional unit representing a share of the remaining space in the grid container. The<span> </span><code>fr</code><span> </span>unit can only be used for the<span> </span><em>maximum</em><span> </span>value in the<span> </span><code>minmax()</code>function.</span><span><span><span> </span></li></ul>

<h2>Key Behaviors</h2>

<ul><li><span><strong>Invalid Range</strong>: If the specified<span> </span><code>max</code><span> </span>value is less than the<span> </span><code>min</code><span> </span>value (e.g.,<span> </span><code>minmax(200px, 100px)</code>), the<span> </span><code>max</code>value is ignored, and the function is treated as just the<span> </span><code>min</code><span> </span>value.</span></li><li><span><strong>Responsive Grids</strong>: A common use case is creating responsive grids with the<span> </span><code>repeat()</code><span> </span>and<span> </span><code>auto-fit</code><span> </span>or<span> </span><code>auto-fill</code><span> </span>keywords:</span><div><div><div><div><div>css</div></div><div><pre><code><span>grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(</span><span>200px</span><span>, </span><span>1fr</span><span>));</span></code></pre></div></div><div>




This creates as many columns as will fit, each at least<span> </span><code>200px</code><span> </span>wide and growing to take an equal fraction (<code>1fr</code>) of the available space if more space exists.</span></li><li><span><strong>Not the same as<span> </span><code>min()</code><span> </span>and<span> </span><code>max()</code>:<span> </span><code>minmax()</code><span> </span>defines a<span> </span><em>range</em><span> </span>for grid tracks only, while the<span> </span><code>min()</code><span> </span>and<span> </span><code>max()</code>mathematical functions can be used for various CSS properties to select the smallest or largest of a list of values, respectively</span></li></ul>
